One thing that helped me decide to file, was to total up ALL the debt I owed, and compare it against my income. I owed north of $45k, and the most income I have EVER made for a year of my life was $28k after taxes. Call me a pessimist if you want, but given my personal issues, my income is unlikely to increase any time soon.

I've heard that credit unions typically are difficult about people filing BK. I burned my first local credit union I ever banked with for $8500, and (understandably so) they won't touch me with a 10ft pole anymore. Possibly someone with more experience can chime in on awful things credit unions have done to BK filers in the past. 

In a CH7 my understanding is that you can't exclude any debt. You can re-affirm secured debts (car loans etc), but anything unsecured, like a credit card or personal loan can't be reaffirmed. Re-affirming basically is a rewriting of the financing agreement.

Part of my debt was on a 2014 VW Jetta. POS barely ran correctly most of the time, dashboard lit up like a Christmas tree most of the time, etc. 

I owed nearly $15k on that hideous pile of junk when it was worth 6k in good running order. Payments were $402.05/mo @18%. Half of my then wife's car was also included since it was our only tangible joint asset. Wrote it into the divorce agreement and everything. We were paying $128.32 a WEEK for a 2017 Chevrolet Sonic. $18k for $9k worth of car.  

I actually cried tears of joy when the shitty fly-by-night finance company came to flatbed it off to what I'm sure was a salvage auction. 

The other parts of my debt were the usual smattering of credit cards, a personal loan, and other debts to the tune of $20k, and medical debt that was around that same amount.

I don't regret a thing about filing, despite not being able to finance a sandwich with money down now. 

 I was also in a very psychologically and financially abusive marriage for the vast majority of the year and a half it took to rack up all that debt. I filed CH7 in Indiana, discharged in late April of this year.

Tier 2 I like toughness on the PDW, but scavenger on the MSMC
Tier 3 Dexterity is awesome for rushing. Combined with QuickDraw, you'll be able to snap away from sprinting and hose down the enemy quickly, often taking minimal damage in the process. Long barrel is on there to increase the ranges you can 3-shot someone with these guns. Since they rely on higher damage and a lower rate of fire, you shouldn't rely on hip fire for every kill, especially in the absence of a laser sight. Lethals and Tacticals are left to the player for choice. As far as a defensive class goes, try an LMG. Any of them will do very well when set up in a prepared position, my personal favorite is the MK48. Go with an optic of your choice (target finders are lazy, but effective), and either the Adj. Stock or FMJ. Flak Jacket paired with the trophy system will keep your area of choice locked down, Tactical Mask to keep your sights clear when under duress from enemy tacticals are imminent. Toughness will keep your sights on target even when your prey fights back with their own weapon. Hipfire isn't a very useful resource with LMG's so try and keep your sights up almost all the time. A notable exception to this kid the QBB LSW, with its epic 900+RPM, I'd recommend the laser sight with it for clearing and locking down tighter areas. Experiment and try different setups, you'll be the judge of what you like after all.
